title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 10 (Effect of Memorandum and Articles)

content.overview: Section 10 provides that the memorandum and articles, when registered, bind the company and the members to the same extent as if they had been signed by the company and by each member and contained covenants on the part of the company and each member to observe their provisions.
content.glance: State that registered memorandum and articles bind the company and members as contractual covenants; note the inter se nature of the obligation.
content.study: Section 10 gives the memorandum and articles contractual force between the company and its members and among the members inter se. Once registered, they operate as if signed by the company and each member and as containing covenants to observe all their provisions. This underpins the members’ rights to enforce the constitution and the company’s power to enforce compliance by members. Outsider rights generally require a separate contract; the statutory contract under s. 10 is primarily internal. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in s. 10 and link to ss. 4 and 5.

sections.heading: Binding Effect on Company and Members
sections.body: Registered memorandum and articles bind the company and each member as if signed by them and containing covenants to observe their provisions.

sections.heading: Inter Se Nature
sections.body: The statutory contract operates between the company and members and among members inter se.

sections.heading: Enforcement
sections.body: Members may enforce constitutional rights; the company may enforce member obligations under the articles.

examples.title: Member enforcement
examples.body: A member seeks to restrain the company from acting contrary to a provision of the articles. Section 10 supports the binding force of the articles inter se.

examples.title: Outsider claim
examples.body: A third party who is not a member seeks to enforce an article for personal benefit. Section 10 does not by itself create outsider rights; a separate contract is required.

hypotheticals.question: Do the articles bind a person who is not a member?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 10 creates a statutory contract among the company and members. Outsiders generally need a separate contractual or statutory basis.

hypotheticals.question: Can the company enforce articles against a member?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 10 treats the articles as covenants by each member to observe their provisions.

distinctions.title: Internal statutory contract vs outsider rights
distinctions.left: s. 10 binds company and members inter se
distinctions.right: Outsiders need separate contract or statute

misconceptions.trap: Articles automatically bind every person who deals with the company.
misconceptions.correction: Section 10 creates an internal statutory contract; outsider rights require a separate basis.

misconceptions.trap: Memorandum and articles have no contractual force.
misconceptions.correction: Section 10 expressly gives them binding effect as if signed and containing covenants.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 10 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State the binding effect. II. Identify company/member parties. III. Distinguish outsider claims. IV. Conclude on enforceability.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Registration status of memo/articles; parties bound; inter se analysis; outsider issue if any; precise relief.
